claim: Manual picking of structures of interest is very precise but very time-consuming.

source: To prepare a training dataset for this latter model, we opened all 101 tomograms in Ais and browsed the data to select and annotate slices where one or multiple antibody-C1 complexes were clearly visible (Figure 4A). The training dataset thus consisted of samples taken from multiple different tomograms; the annotation and data selection in this case took around 1 hr of work.
evidence: This is data about the time required for annotation.

claim: A batch segmentation process of 3 models × 156 tomograms was launched and left to complete overnight.

claim: Ais was used to inspect the segmented volumes and original datasets in 3D, and the threshold value was adjusted to minimize false positive particles.

claim: Particle picking in Ais comprises thresholding segmented volumes at a user-specified level.

claim: A distance transform of the binary volume is computed in particle picking.
source: Second, a distance transform of the resulting binary volume is computed, in which every nonzero pixel in the binary volume is assigned a new value, equal to the distance of that pixel to the nearest zero-valued pixel in the mask.
evidence: This describes a step in the particle picking algorithm.

claim: A watershed transform is applied to the distance transformed volume in particle picking.
source: Third, a watershed transform is applied to the resulting volume, so that the sets of pixels closest to any local maximum in the distance transformed volume are assigned to one group.
evidence: This describes a step in the particle picking algorithm.

claim: Groups smaller than a user-specified minimum volume are discarded in particle picking.
source: Fourth, groups that are smaller than a user-specified minimum volume are discarded.
evidence: This describes a step in the particle picking algorithm.

claim: The remaining groups are assigned a weight value equal to the sum of the prediction value of the pixels in the group.
source: Fifth, the remaining groups are assigned a weight value, equal to the sum of the prediction value (i.e. the corresponding pixel value in the input.mrc volume) of the pixels in the group.
evidence: This describes a step in the particle picking algorithm.

claim: For every group found within close proximity to another group, the group with the lower weight value is discarded.
source: For every group found within close proximity to another group (using a user-specified value for the minimum particle spacing), the group with the lower weight value is discarded.
evidence: This describes a step in the particle picking algorithm.

claim: The centroid coordinate of the grouped pixels is considered the final particle coordinate.
source: Finally, the centroid coordinate of the grouped pixels is considered the final particle coordinate, and the list of all coordinates is saved in a tab-separated text file with values rounded to the nearest integer.
